reason: This passage (1 Chronicles 11) is narrated from a third-person historical perspective focused on elite figures and leadership. The narrative concentrates on David's ascension to kingship, his covenant with the elders of Israel, the capture of Jerusalem, and detailed accounts of his mighty men (gibborim) and their heroic exploits. While regular people ('all Israel,' the Jebusites) are mentioned, they function as background or collective participants rather than as the perspective from which the story is told. The detailed narrative attention is devoted to David, his military commanders (Joab, Abishai, Benaiah, etc.), and their valor in battle—not to the experiences or viewpoints of ordinary working people.
